title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 1 at Steelers Post Game Press Conference | Atlanta Falcons
headline: Falcons lost at Pittsburgh with Cooper Rush starting; Bijan Robinson's 173-yard day is the main positive, while Penix and Tua injury timelines remain unclear and Kyle Pitts left early with tests pending.
summary: Stefanski credited Pittsburgh but said penalties, turnovers, and a defensive touchdown made the road loss hard to overcome, and that the team needs to turn practice reps into game execution. He said the penalties appeared to be mostly post-snap, with some technique issues and some plays where players were beaten quickly and resorted to holding. He said Cooper Rush had only two days of preparation, but the team kept plenty of the original game plan. On the pass rush, he said protection is a team responsibility and that the offensive line shouldn't take all the blame. Bijan Robinson was praised for his running, with Stefanski saying the team will keep leaning on him and needs to find ways to get all its players touches. Za'Darius Smith received many reps, and several new players, including Yasir Abdullah, are still being sorted into roles. Stefanski said Jack Strand was not an option to play because Rush was healthy, and praised Strand's development. He gave no timeline on Michael Penix Jr. or Tua Tagovailoa, and said Kyle Pitts left early with tests pending. The team moves on quickly to a division opponent next week.

injuries.detail: Asked for an update on when Mike could return; Stefanski said he had no update.
Asked for an update on when Tua could return; Stefanski said he had no update.
Left the game early; Stefanski said tests are pending and long-term status is not yet known.

He said pass protection is a team responsibility, including receivers and backs, and that Pittsburgh's rushers were excellent, though the team can still do better.
Stefanski said the defense did well limiting Pittsburgh on third downs, holding them to a low conversion rate, which he credited to the rush and coverage.
The Falcons knew Pittsburgh's top corner might be inactive and waited until gameday to confirm, but did not give details about how it affected the game plan.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps His First Regular-Season Win as Head Coach
headline: Derrick Henry (three TDs) and Chris Moore (career-high 174 all-purpose yards after activation) headline the Week 1 win; the receiver injury update is still unclear.
summary: Minter opened by praising the team after the 41-23 win over the Colts, calling it the first real chance to show the team they want to be and crediting Indianapolis as a good football team. He said the offense started strong, singled out Declan Doyle's debut and the offensive line, and credited Lamar Jackson for running the operation. He admitted the defense struggled on the first drive before settling in and attacking the football. On the closing drive, he said the offensive line took over and the team was able to grind out a six-minute possession to end the game. He praised Derrick Henry's three touchdowns as typical of his preparation and work habits, and he credited the players, not the play-calling, for the early sharpness. On the injury front, he had no real update on the receiver who appeared to have a hand issue, and he highlighted Chris Moore's career-high 174 all-purpose yards after the team activated him, noting the depth at receiver with a 70-man roster. He said his confidence in kicker Tyler Loop never wavered despite preseason misses. Finally, he credited Roquan Smith's second-drive interception with flipping momentum and Marlon Humphrey for his turnover-forcing ability. He said the team now needs to settle into a normal weekly routine and stay true to its identity.

injuries.player: Unidentified receiver (transcribed as 'Jacoby', possibly hand/cast injury)
injuries.detail: Asked about a receiver who seemed to have a cast on his hand after leaving the game; Minter had no real update and said they'd see how it looks.

signals.note: Three rushing or receiving touchdowns in the opener is a strong fantasy start and reinforces his workload in a short-handed receiver group.

signals.quote: Major shout out to Chris Moore though.

signals.note: A turnover-producing linebacker with a defensive play that changed the game gives him IDP and defensive value for the week.
signals.quote: Roquan sort of flipped the momentum for us

signals.note: Minter framed Humphrey's forced turnovers as a long-term trait, which supports his IDP and defensive-turnover upside.

Minter admitted the defense struggled early but said it settled in and attacked the football; the team also called a fourth-down play that the players wanted to run.

title: Joe Brady Talks His First Victory As An NFL Head Coach
headline: Brady's first win as head coach: Kincaid and DJ Moore are big in the offense, Josh Allen trusts his weapons, and Dalton Kincaid's health is the thing to monitor before a short week against Detroit.
summary: Brady called the 36-31 win over Houston a good first step in year one and said he was proud of the team's conviction, adding that there is no such thing as an ugly win. He said the offense did well getting the ball in its hands in key moments, though the run game needed to be better and the team had mistakes, including a sack early, a critical three-and-out, and a close interception. He praised the defense for limiting Houston's edge rushers and forcing two takeaways, and said the unit wants to play in two-minute situations. He credited DJ Moore's down-field ability and said his impact opens things up for everyone, and he praised Kincaid's matchup value and his improved strength in the run game. On Kincaid's health, Brady said he is more on the field when he is healthy and that he is getting his body ready for the coming days. He said Josh Allen trusts his weapons, that he told Allen to trust the play call and take the open look, and that the aggressive throw to Josh Palmer on the late drive was the right decision. Brady said the offensive line and the whole team protected Allen well, with help from backs, receivers, and tight ends. He stressed that the mistakes must be cleaned up quickly because the short turnaround means there is no time to dwell on the win.

injuries.detail: Has struggled to stay healthy and is working through knee confidence; Brady said he is getting his body ready 'for in a couple days' but gave no formal status.

signals.claim: Will continue to be a key down-field weapon and opens up the offense for other players.
signals.note: Strong debut with big-play production and a clear role as a top target in Buffalo's offense.
signals.quote: He opens us up. He opens it up for everybody right.

signals.claim: Will be on the field more as he stays healthy and has a bigger role in the run game and matchups.
signals.note: Brady called him a matchup problem who is stronger in the run game, suggesting a larger workload if he stays healthy.
signals.quote: He's only going to allow us to get him on the field a little more.

signals.claim: Body is being readied for the short week, with no clear health status given.
signals.note: Knee history plus the short turnaround before Detroit makes his availability and snap count a real question.
signals.quote: excited for him to now just get the body ready to go

signals.claim: Trusted by Josh Allen in key late-game moments and will keep getting targets when his route is open.
signals.note: Allen threw him the aggressive late-drive ball, so he has trust in pressure situations.
signals.quote: Josh Palmer man trusted. And that's kind of who we have to be.

signals.claim: Has embraced a new position and scheme role and will be used in more specific spots as he gets comfortable.
signals.note: Brady said the scheme fits him and he will get more comfortable, which could mean more defensive snaps and sacks upside. Player identity is inferred from the context (Chubb and Ed Oliver).

signals.note: Allen's confidence in his targets and the protection he received support a strong passing outlook.
signals.quote: a lot of trust that Josh has in those guys.

topics.detail: Brady praised the defense for finishing the game, limiting Houston's edge rushers, and forcing two takeaways, but said the unit and special teams need cleanup before Detroit.
The line and the whole offense received credit for protecting Allen, with one early sack the main issue.
Brady stressed that the mistakes from this game must be fixed quickly because the next game comes on a short turnaround.

title: Dave Canales on Week 1 game vs. Bears
headline: Canales praised Bryce Young's rhythm and playmaking but gave no timeline on Bobby Brown, who left and returned during the Week 1 loss to the Bears.
summary: Canales called the season-opening loss to Chicago disappointing, citing 17 points off turnovers, fundamental mistakes, penalties that extended Bears drives, and missed chances to turn field goals into touchdowns. He said the defense's breakdown needs film review before he will make any declarations, and that the issue looked like execution and players stepping out of their responsibilities rather than a lack of toughness. He said the offense found some balance and explosive plays, with Brad calling a rhythmic game, and he backed the call on the failed fourth-down attempt. Bryce Young got particular praise for extending plays with his legs and hitting deep throws, including to Jalen Coker. On the defensive line, Canales said Bobby Brown was working through something and returned, and he promised more information later. He defended Derrick Brown, who he said was sick about the offsides and roughing-the-passer penalty, and he said the team must play more consistently. Canales took responsibility for the group's performance and said the team did not play well enough in any phase to win.

injuries.detail: Left and returned multiple times while appearing to be in pain; Canales said he is 'working through some stuff' and more information will come later, but he bounced back and finished the game.

signals.claim: Showed a strong rhythm and extended plays, so his performance is worth building on going forward.
signals.note: Canales praised Young's rhythm, legs, and deep throws, which supports his fantasy floor in the passing game.

signals.note: Coker was singled out for deep throws, a positive sign for his downfield role, though Canales did not discuss his usage further.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' performance vs. Panthers in season opener | Press Conference
headline: Bears' run game and Caleb Williams' start looked strong; Coach Johnson praised D'Andre Swift after his extension and said no injury concerns came up.
summary: Coach Ben Johnson said the Bears came out of the 59-37 win over Carolina relatively unscathed and credited preparation for handling the heat. He highlighted the takeaways, especially a muffed punt that set up a quick offensive score, and said the defense also made big plays. He called the offensive line and tight ends the story of the game, with the rushing attack controlling it, and praised Swift and Monangai. On Caleb Williams, Johnson said he came out hot, showed quick decisions and checkdowns, and handled the quarterback meeting well, though there were things to fix on tape. Johnson said he'd like to have a better-looking first half on offense and felt the team stayed composed after an early drive setback. He defended the fourth-and-two attempt from his own 21 as a game-specific decision and said the goal is to lead the league in scoring. He ended by saying the team must improve in all three phases each week.

signals.note: Johnson's praise and the rushing success point to Swift being a key part of the backfield plan.

signals.note: Johnson's praise and mention of his rushing ability support Williams as a multi-faceted fantasy option.

signals.quote: Swift and Monangai both were able to do a great job there.

signals.note: Johnson described the sideline catch as typical of him, which supports his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: that's who he is and that's what he does.

signals.note: The end-zone score adds to Kmet's red-zone target value.

Johnson defended going for it on fourth-and-two from the team's 21, saying the decision depended on the game situation and that the team wants to lead the league in scoring.
Johnson said the team must improve in all three phases, that the tape will be reviewed, and that the coming schedule gets harder.

title: Zac Taylor: "Excited For The Win" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Burrow's chemistry with Mike Gesicki and Tee Higgins in the late-game passing is a standout, and Taylor praised Bryan Cook and the defense for four turnovers in the Week 1 win over Tampa Bay.
summary: Taylor called the 33-27 Week 1 win over Tampa Bay a good result that still has plenty to correct. He credited the team's late-game finish, a three-to-four minute situational drill the team had practiced for a long time, and the defense's four turnovers, which produced about 24 points. He praised the kicker for four field goals and said the home crowd was a real weapon, pointing to Tampa Bay's false starts and delay-of-game penalties early. On the offense, Taylor said Mike Gesicki is a player he always counts on, with Joe Burrow giving him a green light to adjust routes, and that Tee Higgins's catch on second and ten was the kind of play Burrow trusted him to make. Taylor said Burrow managed the game well, that the offensive line handled a difficult Tampa Bay blitz package, and that Chase Brown was effective against man coverage. He also praised the young defensive players, including Demetrius Knight and Bryan Cook, and said Cook was motivated playing near his Cincinnati hometown. The team faces a tough road game next week.

signals.claim: Gesicki is a trusted target whom Burrow gets a green light to adjust routes for
signals.note: Taylor's comments suggest Gesicki has a freelancing role in the passing game and in late-game and red-zone situations, which supports his fantasy value.
signals.quote: I always count on Mike. He's got great awareness to break off routes

signals.claim: Burrow trusts Higgins to make the high-difficulty slant play in key situations
signals.note: Taylor called Higgins's catch as big as you'll see and said Burrow chose it from two sideline options, so he is trusted in clutch spots.
signals.quote: Joe trusts him. He sees the look.

signals.claim: Brown is effective against man coverage and was used in situational drives
signals.note: Taylor said Brown's ability to make defenders miss and convert first downs against man coverage was a key part of the closing drive.
signals.quote: Chase Brown does a great job versus man coverage.

signals.claim: Burrow managed the game well and delivered in the tough late-game looks
signals.note: Taylor's praise of Burrow's decision-making and his chemistry with Gesicki and Higgins supports continued high passing volume.
signals.quote: performance on Joe really good

signals.claim: Cook made splash plays, including a forced fumble and a fumble recovery
signals.note: Cook's turnover production and extra motivation from playing near home make him a strong IDP and defensive-play candidate.
signals.quote: be cook plays with, like a little different chip on his shoulder

signals.claim: Knight made a big play early that finished a scoring sequence and boosted momentum
signals.note: Taylor praised the young defender's growth and playmaking, which suggests a bigger defensive role going forward.
signals.quote: they're playing faster. And they got great guys around them

topics.detail: The defense forced four turnovers that led to about 24 points. Taylor said the team will correct mistakes after the win, and he credited the defensive line with the pressure.
Taylor said the team's situational drill and clock management in the final minutes went as planned, including a drawn offside penalty and a quarterback sneak to finish.
Taylor said the home crowd helped by forcing Tampa Bay into false starts and a delay-of-game penalty, and he called the crowd a weapon.
Taylor credited the offensive line for handling Tampa Bay's blitz package, and he gave Baker Mayfield credit for escaping several tough pressure situations.
Taylor praised the kicker for four field goals and said the team's kicking gave them confidence in fourth-down decisions.
Taylor said the team has a tough road game next week and will prepare to correct the issues from this game.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Jaguars: September 13th, 2026
headline: Monken blames the coaching and execution for a lopsided opening loss, won't commit to Deshaun Watson for Tampa until he reviews the tape, and says Zion Johnson's ankle status is unclear.
summary: Monken called the loss on the road a failure of both players and coaching, pointing to operational problems like delay-of-game and false-start penalties, and a slow start with three-and-outs after a turnover on the opening drive. He said the offense couldn't sustain drives or get off the field on third down, and that he takes ownership as head coach. On Deshaun Watson, he repeatedly said the criticism wasn't all on him, defended his arm and effort, and said the interception was not a tentative throw. He would not say whether Watson starts next week in Tampa, saying he hadn't watched the tape and that the quarterback is one of 53 players on the roster, with every position to be evaluated. He praised the rookies (Spencer Fano, Austin Barber, Denzel Boston and others) as future standouts while acknowledging the moment was too big for none of them in terms of execution. On Zion Johnson, he said Johnson returned to the game after going down with an ankle injury and that the team would check on him Monday. He also said the team had been preparing for noise and heat, but that nothing replicates a real game, and framed the season as a 17-game journey.

injuries.detail: Went down with an ankle injury, returned to the game; Monken said the team will see how he feels tomorrow.

signals.claim: Starting role for next week in Tampa is undecided pending film review
signals.note: Monken would not commit to Watson for Week 2, so the starting job is an open question until the staff reviews the tape.

signals.claim: Interception was not a sign of tentative play, according to the coach
signals.note: Monken rejected the idea that Watson was playing tentatively, which suggests his aggressiveness is not in question, but the turnover and drive stalls still need fixing.
signals.quote: He let that ball rip. That was an interception.

signals.note: Johnson returned to the game after a scary ankle injury, but the coach said he will only know his status after checking him the next day.
signals.quote: We'll have to see tomorrow when he gets back in.

signals.quote: Casey and Denzel are going to be tremendous players.

signals.note: Fano started on the offensive line as a rookie, and Monken's praise suggests he's firmly in the starting group going forward.
signals.quote: I think Spencer is going to be a tremendous player.

topics.detail: Monken cited delay-of-game and false-start penalties, plus substitution and huddle issues and late play calls, as major problems to fix before Wednesday.
The defense subbed early because of the heat and the offense's short drives, which kept the unit on the field too long; Monken said depth and rotation need work.
Four rookies started on offense, and Monken said the moment wasn't too big for them, though he's still reviewing the film.
Monken called Tampa-bound preparation a chance to fix mistakes and said the team needs to own its mistakes and get better quickly.

title: Campbell on Lions Week 1 performance
headline: Gibbs' 24 carries before OT drew workload questions, but Campbell said he's in the best shape of his tenure and will monitor him; Tay Martin, Barnes and Hutchinson earned praise.
summary: Campbell credited the Saints for playing hard and said the Lions' players stepped up in waves, with the defense forcing three takeaways that turned into points. He praised St. Brown and Gibbs for big performances, said the offensive line blocked well despite some inconsistency, and singled out Hutchinson, Derrick Barnes, and Tay Martin on special teams. On Gibbs, he said the 24 carries were because the back was the hot hand and in excellent shape, but he didn't want to set workload records and said they will monitor him. He said the offense fizzled in the first half and the team needs to be more efficient, and that the Saints' passing game exposed some mental lapses in the secondary that need tightening, though he wasn't concerned. He said he considered going for it at the end of regulation but chose to drain the clock and give the defense the chance to win. Campbell said a scan on a player's hip came back negative but the situation is not resolved. The Lions face Buffalo next on a short week.

signals.claim: Workload of 24 carries before overtime will be monitored going forward; not a goal to set carry records
signals.note: A 24-carry Week 1 workload projects heavy volume, but the coach is signaling he will manage it, so expect some uncertainty about future touch counts.
signals.quote: He's the best shape I've seen since he's been here.

signals.claim: Had a big-time performance in Week 1
signals.note: Campbell singled him out as a standout in the win, a good sign for his target and production expectations.
signals.quote: Gibbs had some really big time performances for us.

signals.claim: Was a difference maker on special teams in Week 1
signals.note: A special-teams standout could carry a role beyond special teams and adds some fantasy relevance in a deep-roster context.
signals.quote: he was a difference maker today.

signals.claim: Was all over the field in the win
signals.note: Campbell's praise suggests a strong defensive role in Week 1, a positive sign for his usage.
signals.quote: Derrick Barnes was all over the field.

signals.claim: Played really well in Week 1
signals.note: Positive review of a key pass rusher supports strong expectations for his defensive production.

topics.detail: Campbell said the defense forced three takeaways that were huge, and the run defense shut down the Saints' running game. He acknowledged the secondary got strung out and needs to tighten mental errors and communication on some plays.

The offense possessed the ball well in the first half but then fizzled and needs to be more efficient. The offensive line blocked well with some inconsistency, and the team rushed for 160 yards while nearly breaking a few more runs open.

Campbell considered going for it at the end of regulation but chose to drain the clock and trust the defense. He said he understood the Saints going for two at the end and that the two-point stop was key.
Campbell said a scan on a player came back negative but the issue is not fully resolved; the player was not named clearly in the transcript, so the affected player is unclear.
The team plays Buffalo next on a short week; Campbell noted Buffalo will also be on a short week.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans vs Bills, Missed Opportunities | Full Q&A
headline: Henry To'oTo'o is being evaluated for a shoulder injury after leaving before the final drive; Ryans praised David Montgomery and Woody Marks as a running back tandem.
summary: Ryans credited Buffalo for winning Week 1 and said Houston's defense missed too many chances to make plays, giving up explosive passes and failing to take the ball away. He said the offense drove consistently and gave the team more than enough points, but two Houston turnovers versus none for Buffalo decided the game. He praised C.J. Stroud for calm, confident control of the offense, while acknowledging the two turnovers. He said David Montgomery ran well and that the offensive line controlled the line of scrimmage in short-yardage situations, and he called Woody Marks's play good too, describing the pair as a one-two punch he likes. On defense, he said Buffalo neutralized the defensive line early, the line got better in the second half, and the coverage and rush need to work together more tightly. He said Henry To'oTo'o is being evaluated for a shoulder injury and more information will come over the next couple of days. He said the Bengals and Joe Burrow are not the focus yet and will be addressed this week.

injuries.detail: Left the game before the final drive with a shoulder injury; Ryans said the team is still evaluating him and will provide more information over the next couple of days.

signals.claim: Montgomery remains a featured part of the Texans' running back committee alongside Woody Marks.
signals.note: Ryans said Montgomery did an outstanding job, which supports his workload in the backfield.
signals.quote: David ran it well.

signals.claim: Marks is part of a two-back rotation with David Montgomery.
signals.note: Ryans called Marks and Montgomery a one-two punch he is happy with, suggesting a shared backfield workload.
signals.quote: Woody also ran it well.

signals.claim: Stroud kept control of the offense and is showing growth and confidence.
signals.note: Ryans praised his poise and decision-making, though the two turnovers are a concern for fantasy consistency.
signals.quote: CJ was very much in control the entire game.

topics.detail: Ryans said the defense missed multiple chances to make plays, gave up too many explosive plays, and needs to cover and finish better. He said Buffalo's line neutralized the Texans' defensive line early before the line got more pressure in the second half.
Ryans said Houston lost the turnover battle 2-0, which he identified as the difference in the game, and noted Buffalo turned those turnovers into points.
Ryans said the team was not in position for Josh Allen's first-half scramble touchdown because players were not tied together and no one had eyes on the quarterback.

title: Liam Coen Recaps Dominant Victory Over Browns: "A True Team Win" | Press Conference
headline: Jaguars' 34-10 Week 1 win was a balanced attack: Trevor Lawrence spread the ball, rookie Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange scored, and the run game was physical.
summary: Coen praised Parker Washington's diving touchdown, calling it a strong route and catch against man coverage with good protection. He said Trevor Lawrence spread the ball around, trusted his playmakers, and ran the offense well, including off-schedule plays and a back-of-the-end-zone touchdown throw. Coen was pleased with the fast start and said the team played more physically, with the defense performing well and the special teams needing cleanup on kickoffs. He said the team showed its own brand of football rather than playing the opponent's game, and that the locker room is tight. He credited Josh Cameron's contested catches and touchdown as a sign of trust from the quarterbacks, and said Brenton Strange's touchdown came because Coen wanted to get him involved. He praised the running back (transcribed as "Basil") for physical, yards-after-contact running and said he trusted his reads. Coen explained Lawrence's fast start came from earlier opener preparation and a clearer game plan. Coen did not discuss injuries or the next opponent.

signals.claim: Parker Washington made an early diving touchdown and was a featured early target
signals.note: Early-game targets and red-zone production add fantasy value for a secondary receiver.
signals.quote: A heck of a play.

signals.claim: Lawrence spread the ball around and trusted playmakers, with the offense built to keep him comfortable
signals.note: A multi-target distribution suggests a solid, if shared, passing-game floor.
signals.quote: I thought he spread the ball around.

signals.claim: Cameron's contested catches and touchdown earned quarterback trust, and he will be a bigger part of the offense
signals.note: A rookie earning contested-catch targets and a touchdown is a strong early fantasy sign.
signals.quote: Josh just continued to put that on tape.

signals.claim: Strange was targeted deliberately and scored a touchdown on the next drive
signals.note: Coen said he wanted to get Strange involved, which supports tight end usage.
signals.quote: I want to get Brenton involved.

signals.claim: Running back ran physically, handled contact well, and was trusted on reads
signals.note: Strong yards-after-contact and a trusted role support his workload and fantasy floor.
signals.quote: I thought he ran nasty.

topics.detail: The offense spread the ball across receivers, backs, and tight ends. Coen said the team mixed run and pass to keep the defense off balance.
Coen praised the defense for a physical effort, holding Cleveland to three points on a short-field scenario and generating pressure on the quarterback.
Coen said the kickoff coverage and kicking game need cleanup, though the defense made the kicks costly for Cleveland.

title: Postgame Press Conference: John Harbaugh on first win as Giants' head coach
headline: Malik Nabers was cleared and played a "great game" in the Week 1 win over Dallas, and Harbaugh praised Jaxson Dart's performance.
summary: Harbaugh opened by crediting the players, the organization, and his faith, and called the Week 1 win over Dallas a team effort in a hard-fought game with a loud, sold-out crowd. He said the win was special because of the players' willingness to bounce back from mistakes. On the end-of-half drive, he credited the offensive game plan and Jaxson Dart's execution while managing the operation, and said the offense answered after Dallas cut the lead. He said the atmosphere exceeded his expectations and that the team must earn that kind of stadium environment each week. Harbaugh said the team is "on our way" toward his vision, with a lot of work still to do. He called the pass protection stellar and said the offensive line could be the best position group in the game, possibly tied with the defensive line. On Malik Nabers, Harbaugh said Nabers was medically cleared, tested himself about two and a half to three hours before kickoff, and played well after he felt ready. Harbaugh also said he trusts the players and that Holland's interception return touchdown was a major swing that helped the team take command in the second half.

injuries.detail: Medically cleared; went out about 2.5-3 hours before kickoff, felt ready, and played a great game.

signals.claim: Cleared medically and played in Week 1 after a pre-game self-test.
signals.note: A clean return from injury with a strong performance means he appears fully available for upcoming weeks.
signals.quote: He played a great game.

signals.claim: Managed a heavy offensive workload and made difficult throws, executing the game plan well.
signals.note: Harbaugh's praise for his command and accuracy supports his confidence as the starter in fantasy lineups.
signals.quote: just tremendous and very impressive.

signals.claim: Made an interception that Harbaugh described as a key turnaround play leading to a touchdown.
signals.note: A defensive takeaway returned for a touchdown is a notable big-play boost for IDP and defensive scoring formats.
signals.quote: here comes Javon Holland out of nowhere like a lightning bolt

topics.detail: Harbaugh called the pass protection outstanding and said the offensive line may be the best position group in the game, possibly tied with the defensive line.
Harbaugh emphasized humility, faith, and team effort, and said the crowd and stadium atmosphere exceeded his expectations.
Harbaugh said the team's strong third-down rate came from a mix of execution, coaching, playmaking, and quarterback play.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference | Jets at Titans (9/13)
headline: Glenn says Breece Hall topped 100 rushing yards with a TD, Kenyon Sadiq scored on the opening drive, and Geno Smith's efficiency was praised; Cooper (ankle) and an unclear groin injury are being monitored.
summary: Glenn opened by calling the Titans win a good start but said penalties and end-of-half situations need cleaning up before the Green Bay game. He said the injuries are a groin issue for a player the transcript calls 'Mika' and an ankle issue for Omar Cooper Jr., and that he is not too worried about either but will update during the week. He credited the offensive line and the run game, citing a 100-plus yard rushing day with a touchdown, and was frustrated that a Braelon Allen touchdown was taken away. He praised the defense's discipline and said coordinator Duke, who ran the defense while Glenn handled other duties, did a strong job. On offense, he stressed explosive plays as a key to winning and said the team missed some chances in the second half. He praised Geno Smith's efficiency and said Kenyon Sadiq's first-drive touchdown was a good moment for a rookie. He explained the end-of-half decision to avoid a risky Hail Mary, and said he did not intend to run a play at six seconds. He also said kicker Sanders did well apart from one miss.

injuries.detail: Groin injury; Glenn said more information will come during the week and he is not too worried.
Ankle injury; Glenn said he is not too worried and will provide updates through the week.

signals.claim: Ran for over 100 yards and a touchdown in the Titans game, a strong rushing output the coach credited to the line.
signals.note: A 100-yard rushing game with a score in the opener supports a featured running back role heading into Green Bay.
signals.quote: Bruce had like 100 and some yards, 102 yards and a touchdown.

signals.claim: Ran hard and had a touchdown taken away by penalty.
signals.note: Allen's work was praised, but his role behind Hall remains unclear from this presser.
signals.quote: Braylon, he ran his butt off, too.

signals.claim: Scored a touchdown on the offense's opening drive.
signals.note: A rookie scoring early in the game is a positive sign for his role in the passing and red-zone offense.
signals.quote: it was just good to get him a touchdown, you know?

signals.claim: Played efficiently, made needed deep throws, and avoided big mistakes.
signals.note: Efficiency and deep-ball success are praised, supporting his fantasy floor in the passing game.
signals.quote: He's a damn good player. It's the reason why he's here.

topics.detail: Glenn praised the defense's discipline and communication, and said Duke ran the unit well while Glenn was away from the defensive play-calling.
Kicker Sanders was praised as doing a good job despite one miss, which Glenn said they would review.
Glenn said he did not want a Hail Mary risk with six seconds left and believed a field goal setup was possible with more yardage.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Falcons
headline: McCarthy praised T.J. Watt's game-changing play, said Darnell Washington will get his opportunities, and said Aaron Rodgers' downfield passing is ahead of schedule.
summary: McCarthy called the 20-13 win over Atlanta a relief, especially the first home win, and credited a defense-first effort that set the tone and kept Pittsburgh in control for most of the game. He said the offense was herky-jerky and struggled on third down, and he pointed to special teams communication and a clock-reset issue as things to fix. He called T.J. Watt's play the biggest of the game and said it swung momentum. On Darnell Washington, he said it's early and that the offense has plenty of opportunities for all its pass-catchers, and that he's confident Washington will get his. He said the downfield passing game has been more productive this early in camp than in any offense he's coached, carried over from practice. He said he'd like to run the ball 25-30 times a game, and that the 40 pass attempts came from penalties and long distances. He also said the coaching staff is still managing a returning corner's ramp-up, with a plan to increase his snaps next week.

signals.claim: Made the biggest play of the game, a momentum-swinging highlight
signals.note: Watt's splash play can carry fantasy value in defensive formats, and it reflects his continued impact.
signals.quote: That was clearly the biggest play in the game.

signals.claim: Will get his opportunities in the offense; no specific increase in third-down role promised
signals.note: McCarthy didn't commit to a bigger role, so his usage is still unclear after one game.
signals.quote: I'm confident that Darnell will will get his get his opportunities.

signals.claim: Threw 40 times; McCarthy wants the run game closer to 25-30 carries a game and calls the pass volume an outlier
signals.note: Rodgers' volume could come down if the run game grows, but the downfield shot-play development is a positive for his ceiling.
signals.quote: I definitely would like to be north of 25 each and every week

topics.detail: McCarthy praised the defense for setting the tone, with the only real damage coming from giving up field position. The defense produced multiple sacks and takeaways.
The offense looked inconsistent, with third-down efficiency the main concern. The team had a tough sequence of penalties, and McCarthy said the passing game is ahead of schedule on downfield throws.

A returning corner referred to only as 'Joey' was active for this game and remains on a ramp-up plan, with snaps expected to increase in the coming week. He was not identified by surname in the transcript and does not appear on the provided roster, so no signal was assigned.
McCarthy cited a communication breakdown on resetting the clock and verbal issues as areas to correct before next game.

title: Todd Bowles on Season Opener: Limiting Turnovers | Press Conference
headline: Bucs lost by one score to Cincinnati after four turnovers; Baker Mayfield's ball security is the main concern, Jacob Parrish's back injury is unresolved pending an MRI, and Benjamin Morrison and Josiah Trotter earned praise.
summary: Bowles said the loss came down to turnovers. Tampa Bay had four, including three fumbles by Baker Mayfield, and they lost by one touchdown. He also pointed to missed tackles on short throws that extended Cincinnati drives, false starts, and a late stretch in scoring range where the offense turned it over instead of punting. On Mayfield, Bowles said the fumbles came from holding the ball too long, with one on a scramble he should have gotten rid of and a couple from behind him that he couldn't see, and the staff teaches keeping the ball high and tight. He denied that Bucky Irving's offseason shoulder surgery played any part in Irving's fumble, saying the issue was simply holding onto the ball. Bowles praised Benjamin Morrison, who stepped in after Parrish went down, saying he battled, was composed, and covered well while still having things to learn. Josiah Trotter's pick-six was a play he had rehearsed in practice, and Bowles said it energized the sideline and brought the team within one score. On Parrish, Bowles said he was still pretty sure Parrish would get an MRI the next day and did not yet know the extent of the back injury. He said there were no X-rays that he knew of. Bowles also clarified that the defense was not in a zone-coverage conflict on the Cincinnati touchdown slant; someone simply should have been there.

injuries.detail: Left the game with a back injury; coach expected an MRI the next day but had no update on the diagnosis.

signals.claim: Needs to hold the ball less and get rid of it sooner to cut turnovers.
signals.note: Ball security and decision-making under pressure are now a focus, which matters for his floor and yardage upside.
signals.quote: Obviously you can't turn the ball over.

signals.claim: His fumble was not related to his offseason shoulder surgery, per the coach.
signals.note: Bowles cleared the shoulder as a factor, but Irving's ball security is now a question for his workload.
signals.quote: No, not at all. We just got to hold on to the ball.

signals.claim: Played well in extended action after Parrish's injury and should keep the bigger role.
signals.note: Morrison's steady performance in extended action makes him a possible starter or rotation piece in the secondary.
signals.quote: I thought he battled. He did some good things.

signals.claim: Made a pick-six on a play he had worked on in practice and continued to contribute in run defense.
signals.note: A defensive touchdown and solid run defense point to a larger linebacker role.
signals.quote: It was a good play on his part.

signals.claim: Expected to undergo an MRI on his back, with no diagnosis yet.
signals.note: His availability for Week 2 depends on the MRI results and is not yet known.
signals.quote: I'm still I'm pretty sure he's going to undergo an MRI.

topics.detail: Tampa Bay had four turnovers, several penalties and false starts, and a missed-tackle problem on the defensive side that kept Cincinnati drives alive. Bowles felt the team was not helping itself against a well-coached opponent.
On the two-yard touchdown slant, Bowles said it was zone coverage and not a conflict between Jacob Parrish and Tykee Smith, but someone should have been in position to cover it.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Jeffery Simmons stays in the defensive line rotation's key moments, while Cam Ward's missed throws are a clear concern after the Week 1 loss to the Jets.
summary: Saleh said the Titans were outplayed in all three phases in Week 1, and he expected a better performance. He credited the Jets for a physical first half, a 19-play drive, and a heavy run game that held the ball for about 41 minutes, while the Titans couldn't win the field position battle on punts and allowed explosive passing plays. He said the offense needs to win its one-on-one matchups and that quarterback Cam Ward has to make the throws he missed, which the staff will keep working on with him. On defensive line rotation, Saleh acknowledged that the Jets gained yards on runs while Simmons was off the field, but said he will review the tape and still wants Simmons in third-down, two-minute, and late-game situations, so the rotation won't change. He defended the decision not to go for it on fourth down late in the third quarter, saying the percentages were roughly the same and the team needed to manufacture another possession. He said the team is fine, that it is a young group that will improve over the season, and that he remains calm but will look closely at the film before making decisions.

signals.claim: Simmons will stay in the defensive line rotation, with his biggest role in third-down, two-minute, and late-game situations
signals.note: Saleh is keeping the rotation intact but leaning on Simmons in high-leverage snaps, so his total snap count may stay limited while his situational work stays strong.
signals.quote: we need Jeff to be as Jeff in the gotta have it situations

signals.claim: Ward missed several makeable throws and must be more accurate; the staff will keep working with him on it
signals.note: Missed accuracy on makeable throws is a red flag for his efficiency and fantasy floor until he shows improvement.
signals.quote: He's got to make those throws. And he knows that.

topics.detail: Saleh said the Titans were outplayed in all three phases, leaned on by a physical Jets run game, and outpaced in time of possession (about 41 minutes for the Jets). The Titans struggled with the punt game and gave up explosive passing plays in the second half.

Saleh said the Jets used a two-shell look that stopped the Titans' run game, and the team needs to win its one-on-one blocks. The coach took responsibility for the play-calling and alignment that left the run game short.

Saleh said a challenged fumble was close, with the ball coming out just as a foot touched the ground, and the team was slightly off. He defended going for a punt on fourth down late in the third quarter because the team needed to manufacture another possession either way.
Saleh said the team is frustrated but steady, and he is not planning to react emotionally. He acknowledged the boos but said the team's focus is on improving.
A reporter said Jacob Martin got an IV and was evaluated for a concussion, but both he and another player finished the game. Saleh did not comment on this in the transcript, so it is unconfirmed.
